title: No real contradiction: deniers refuse absolute supreme adoration; affirmers mean adoration below the supreme
source_text: XXXIX. Nec est quod quis miretur viros, ita celebres in schola Romana, ut sunt Vasquez, Suarez & Mendoza, aliique non pauci, palam asserere, tanquam veritatem Catholicam, quod Sancti sint adorandi; cum tamen id a plurimis in Ecclesia Romana negetur, multique contra fateantur Deum solum esse adorandum, nec se alium quam Deum adorare. Etenim nulla est inter eos propterea contradictio. Nam qui negant Sanctos esse adorandos, hoc intelligunt de adoratione plane summa & absoluta, qualis soli Deo competit. Qui vero dicunt adorandos esse, istud intelligi volunt de adoratione quadam infra supremam, quam priores isti Sanctis non denegant.
pass_a_gloss: Nor is there reason that anyone wonder that men so celebrated in the Roman school as are Vázquez, Suárez and Mendoza, and not a few others, openly assert as a Catholic truth that the Saints are to be adored; when yet that is denied by very many in the Roman Church, and many on the contrary confess that God alone is to be adored, and that they adore no other than God. For there is no contradiction among them on that account. For those who deny that the Saints are to be adored understand this of plainly supreme and absolute adoration, such as befits God alone. But those who say they are to be adored will that to be understood of a certain adoration below the supreme, which those former ones do not deny to the Saints.
pass_b_english: Famous Jesuits say Saints are to be adored; many Romans say only God is—yet Le Blanc finds no contradiction.
Deniers mean absolute supreme latria; affirmers mean inferior adoration the deniers still allow.

lemmas.gloss: with plainly supreme and absolute adoration
with a certain adoration below the supreme

choices.why: Le Blanc’s reconciling verdict on the School split.
